scenes.title: One offering — yet it took two goats
scenes.atmos: smoke one side, dust and pale light the other
scenes.subject_block: One frame holding the riddle: on the left, the first goat lying still and peacefully at rest on the low altar step, as if asleep, its pale unblemished coat clean and whole, gently lit by warm amber firelight and rising smoke, the pale stone steps beneath it bare and unmarked (the price); on the right, the live goat facing an open pale road into the waste (the guilt carried off); the altar between them a low box-shaped structure of dark acacia wood plated in dull bronze, a small blunt bronze horn projecting from each of its four corners, resting directly on the sand. A single unified canvas, soft transition, no hard divider, calm and reverent, the stone clean, dry and pale throughout.

scenes.title: Every year I came back and did it again
scenes.subject_block: A unified tableau of weary repetition: Aaron, in plain white linen, at the altar, repeated as the SAME one man in soft ghosted echoes receding into the dark — the same act year upon year, not different priests; the same two goats faintly doubled; turning seasons hinted in the sky; the same bronze basin resting closed and still on the altar stone, its contents dark, settled and motionless; the worn altar stone; soft vignettes melting into one dim recurring canvas; nothing dripping, nothing poured, no liquid in motion; no breastplate, no other priests or bearded men. Aaron and every ghosted echo of him are the aged high priest with long gray hair and a full gray beard.

world.era: Wilderness Tabernacle period, c. 1400 BC, the Exodus generation in the Sinai wilderness, the first Day of Atonement.
world.place: In and around the portable Tabernacle — a tent of skins and woven linen curtains in a desert camp, NOT a stone temple: linen court walls, a bronze altar, the veil and the mercy seat, surrounded by bleached wilderness.
world.light: A single warm key light, dawn-gold and oil-lamp flame from the left with deep Caravaggio shadow opposite, softened by incense and dust haze; the same light direction in every scene.
world.palette: Muted earth tones — sand, bone-white linen, ochre, dried-blood red, bronze and deep shadow-brown, with warm gold highlights only; no bright or saturated modern colour.

no stone-temple or cathedral architecture — it is a tent
no modern metal, fabric, objects, chairs or furniture out of period
